Discover New Cliff Dwellings in Zion National Park.

National Park in Utah was re-alled to Evre Powell, of the Union Pacific Press Bureau, yesterday, 800 miles from where the photograph was taken, in enlarging a plate for another purpose. The cave where the buildings are located is on the inaccessible side of a cliff, and was photographed by Mr. Powell from a distance of three-quarters of a mile.

Experts in this line of work yesterday pronounced the discovery a valuable one and believe, because of the location of the buildings and the fact that animals or humans are unable to enter, that discoveries may be made that will reveal the life of the former inhabitants of this region. The city is 500 feet above the nearest ledge and 2500 feet below the top of the cliff in Zion Canyon.

Miss Adelaide Chamberlin of the Southwestern Museum, an authority on the subject, stated yesterday that she believes that invaluable knowledge is to be gained from the discovery. From photographs brought back by Mr. Powell, she stated that evidences of prehistoric peoples are discernible. The ruins are covered with debris, but dwellings and temples are easily identified in the photograph.

An expedition may, be sent from Los Angeles to the canyon and an effort made to scale the cliff. The University of Utah has thought for some time that dwellings existed in the locality, but no effort was made to explore them, it seems. Mr. Powell stated yesterday, that that institution is awaiting word from him regarding his photographs and will undoubtedly send men to investigate.

Many important discoveries have been made in this locality concerning early Indian life. A canyon, six miles from the discovery, has yielded relics that fill several Western museums. The Indian name of Zion Canyon is Mukuntuweap Canyon.
Mr. Powell was sent to the canyon shortly before the signing of the bill

by the President, November 19, creating a national park. He left the railroad at Lund, Utah, and drove 100 miles to the canyon. After exploring for several days he noted a cavity in the cliff which guides said contained a building. It was impossible to climb to the ledge, so he mounted to an equal height on the opposite side of the canyon, three-fourths of a mile distant, and with the aid of a telephoto lens he photographed the side of the cliff.
Nothing more was thought of it

until his return here and he learned that when a nearby cave was enlarged objects appeared which showed signs of human hands. From the location of the cave and the formation it was believed that the photograph had revealed a city that the naked eye had overlooked for centuries, but this was not made positive until yesterday. Mr. Powell plans on returning to the region to explore further, and it is probable some local museum will send men along to secure relics for this city.

BILLY SUNDAY'S TABERNACLE GROUNDS - A CITY SPRUNG UP OVERNIGHT.

This is the site of the Billy Sunday Tabernacle in New York. The biggest undertaking of its kind in the world will open next month when Billy Sunday sounds his first trumpet call in his campaign against the Devil in New York City.
The great Tabernacle has been built on the grounds of the old American League Ball Park at 168th St., and Broadway.

The building cost about $70,000 including the rental of the ground. It will comfortably seat 20,000 people and when New York gets the fever every one of those twenty thousand will be filled to overflowing at every meeting.

The Tabernacle itself is of course the big building of the group. But surrounding it are smaller buildings which will mean much to the thousands who will attend the revivals. There will be an emergency hospital, resting rooms for men and ladies, cafeteria lunch, restaurant, and an independent fire department. There will be checking rooms where babies may be left while Pa and Ma listen to the exhortations of the Rev. William Ashley Sunday.

THE HAUNTED HOUSE WHICH CAUSES
SEASICKNESS.

This is the haunted house near Jacksonville, Fla. that thousands of people have been to see in the last few weeks. It is on the beach at Neptune, which is a continuation of Pablo beach. In a recent storm the front supporting pillars of the house gave way, so that the small structure tilted over at an angle of about 25 degrees at one corner. A negro was sent to remove the furniture and came back ashy with fright, saying the place was "hanted". The flow of the river has actually been held up and then permitted to go on again. It was necessary in building the great dam to held back the Hudson River while 76,50 0 cubic yards of rock were drilled and blasted from the dry bed off the river, in order that slips 360 feet wide and 1,350 feet long lined and sided with concrete, might be built, each one to have a depth of forty-four feet at mean low water. When the War Department (Uncle Sam busses all navigable rivers throughout the land) decided that no pier should extend 1,000 feet into the channel of the Hudson, the Dock Department of New York decided to build anchors. The task was turned over to Rock Commissioner R.A.G.Smith who in turn turned it ever to C.W.Stanford his Chief Engineer. The new piers fill a basin occupying an area of 300 by 930 feet. Tremendous steel cylinders with a new interlocking device were sunk in the soft mud of the river bed, each one composed of seventy-four foot interlocking sheet steel piers$ piles. The cylinders were filled with loam and mud and a bank of rip rap placed along the inshore faces of the cylinders to resist the enormous pressures. As soon as all was completed, a tonch pump was set to wsrk pumping the water from one side of the big barrier to the other.
